new.kārum: dike, embankment (written KAR; Harper kâru): kāršu “his dike”, ina kārišu “in his dike”
new.danānum-D: D-stem of danānum “to be strong”: to strengthen: dunnunim “to strengthen”, udannin “he strengthened”
new.pītum: opening, breach (in a dike): Harper bi-tum
new.petûm-N: N-stem of petûm: to be opened, to open (itself): ittepti “has opened”, ippetû “(which) was opened”
new.ugārum: the irrigated farmland of a district, the commons (written A.GÀR; Harper ugaru)
new.wabālum-Š: Š-stem of wabālum “to carry”: to make (something) carry off: mê uštābil “he let the water carry off”
new.ḫalāqum-D: D-stem of ḫalāqum “to be lost”: to destroy, cause to be lost: uḫalliqu
new.šiqītum: irrigation, watering: ana šiqītim “for irrigation” (Harper ši-ki-tim)
new.šammū: plants, grass, pasture: ana šammī “(to) the plants”
new.akālum-Š: Š-stem of akālum “to eat”: to feed, to let graze: šūkulim “to feed”, uštākil, ušākilu
new.magārum: to agree: itti … imtagar “has come to an agreement with”
new.eṣēdum: to harvest, reap: iṣṣid “he shall harvest”
new.elēnumma: in addition, over and above (Harper e-li-nu-um-ma)
new.elûm-up: to go up, come up: ītelianim “(the sheep) have come up”
new.kannum: band, tie (?): kannū gamartim, a signal hung at the city gate at the end of the grazing season (sense from context)
new.gamartum: completion, end: kannū gamartim “the bands of completion” (?)
new.ḫalālum-N: N-stem of a verb ḫalālum, “to be hung up” (?): ittaḫlalū — the meaning is inferred from the context
new.naṣārum: to guard, keep watch: inaṣṣar “he shall guard”
new.60: sixty — a single vertical wedge (the sexagesimal “one” of the next order, Harper’s LX); said šūši (?)
new.nakāsum: to cut, cut down: ikkis “he cut down”
new.1/2: one half — a horizontal crossed by a vertical (Harper’s ½); said mišil (?) “half (of)”
new.manûm-syll: mina — weight of silver, 60 shekels (about 500 g), here spelled ma-na: 1/2 mana kaspim “half a mina of silver”
new.šaqālum-pres: to weigh out (silver = to pay): išaqqal “he shall pay” (Harper i-ša-ḳal)
new.zaqāpum: to plant (trees), set upright: zaqāpim “to plant” (Harper za-ga-bi-im), izqup “he planted”
new.nukaribbum: gardener, orchard-keeper — written NU.{giš}KIRI₆ “man of the orchard”; Harper leaves it as NU.kirû, later study reads nukaribbum
new.4-kam: four — MU 4{kam}, here a count of years, “four years”, said erbe šanātim (spoken form reconstructed)
new.ḫamuštum: fifth (ordinal): ina ḫamuštim šattim “in the fifth year”
new.zittum: share, portion (written ḪA.LA; Harper zittu): zittašu “his share”
new.nasāqum: to choose, select: inassaq “he shall choose” (Harper i-na-za-ak)
new.gamārum-G: to finish, complete: lā igmur “he did not finish”
new.nidītum: land left lying, an unplanted patch (from nadûm “to leave”)
new.ezēbum-G: to leave, leave behind: īzib “he left”
new.libbum-in: heart, inside: ana libbi “into (the middle of)”
new.šakānum-G: to set, place: išakkanūšum “they shall place for him”
new.nadānum-N2: N-stem of nadānum: to be given: innadnušum “(which) was given to him”
new.šanātum: years (plural of šattum): ša šanātim “of the years”
new.nadûm-N: N-stem of nadûm: to be left lying (of land): innadû “(in which) it lay neglected”
new.epēšum-G: to do, make; to work (land): eqlam šipram ippeš “he shall do the work on the field”
new.ištiat: one (feminine of ištēn): ša šattim ištiat “of one year”
new.rakābum-D: D-stem of rakābum “to ride, mount”: to pollinate (date palms): rukkubim “to pollinate”, urakkib
new.adi-while: until, as long as: adi kirâm ṣabtu “as long as he holds the orchard”
new.ṣabātum-hold: to seize, hold: ṣabtu “(as long as) he holds”
new.biltum-yield: yield (of an orchard), produce: biltam, bilat kirîm “the yield of the orchard”
new.maṭûm-D: D-stem of maṭûm “to be little”: to reduce, diminish: umtaṭṭi “he has reduced” (Harper um-ta-di)

known_used.šumma: if — the word that opens every law of the code
known_used.irrišum: tenant, cultivator: irrišum, ana irrišim “to a tenant”; irrissu “his tenant” (irriš + -šu; Harper reads the same spelling as a verb, “he shall cultivate it”)
known_used.eqlum: field (written A.ŠÀ): eqelšu “his field” — the fief-land this whole block protects
known_used.lū: or; either (lū … lū “whether … or”); with verb: “let …”
known_used.šamaššammū: sesame, the oil-plant: šamaššammam, šamaššammim (written ŠE.GIŠ.Ì; Harper ŠE.IZ.NI)
known_used.bašûm-Š: Š-stem of bašûm “to exist”: to bring into being, produce (a crop): uštabši “he has produced” (perfect)
known_used.enûm: to change, revoke: īteni “he altered”, enêm “altering”
known_used.awīlum: man; the free citizen, the code’s first legal class
known_used.ana: to, for; with infinitive: in order to
known_used.aḫum: arm, side: aḫšu iddi “he let his arm drop” = he was idle, negligent
known_used.nadûm: to cast, throw (a charge; a body into the river): iddi, nadû, iddû · also to leave lying (a field): ittadi “he has left (it) lying”
known_used.leʾûm: to be able: ileʾʾi “he is able” (Harper: i-li-i)
known_used.kaspum: silver — the code’s money, written KÙ.BABBAR “shining precious-metal”
known_used.zâzum: to divide, share: izuzzū “they shall divide”
known_used.petûm: to open; of land, to bring into cultivation: iptete “he has opened”
known_used.itûm: neighbour, the adjoining one: kīma itêšu “like its neighbour” (the neighbouring field)
known_used.madādum: to measure out (grain): imaddad “he shall measure out”
known_used.epšētum: works, tilling: eqel epšētim “a field of works”, a field already prepared
known_used.10: ten — one corner-wedge (U); said ešret (?) with a masculine noun, ešer with a feminine one (Akkadian 3–10 take the opposite gender’s form): 10 ŠE.GUR “ten kor of grain”. Before a field-measure the wedge may count bur-units rather than tens (see §44)
known_used.būrum: the bur, a field measure (written GAN.E; Harper reads GAN, 1,800 SAR, about 6⅔ acres): būrim
known_used.kurrum: the kor, a grain measure (written GUR; Harper: 300 KA): kur šeʾam “a kor of grain”
known_used.abullum: city gate (KÁ.GAL “great door”): abullam uštēṣi “he has taken out through the gate”
known_used.ebūrum: harvest, the crop: ebūrim “of harvest, at harvest” (one logogram, read BURU₁₄; Harper writes ebûrim)
known_used.kirûm: orchard, garden (written {giš}SAR, the KIRI₆ sign): kirāšu “his orchard”
known_used.rabûm-D: D-stem of rabûm: to bring up, raise: urabbāšu “she shall raise him”
known_used.biltum: yield, tribute, rent: nāši biltim “bearer of the yield”, the state tenant (spelled bi-il-tim, or carved with the tribute-sign GUN)
known_used.târum-D: D-stem of târum: to give back: turru “taken away/captured”; utarrūšumma “they shall return (it) to him”
known_used.nidûtum: uncultivated, fallow land — Harper’s reading of KI.KAL (which he also gives as KANKAL); later dictionaries read the logogram as kankallum “hard, uncultivated land”
known_used.šaluštum: one-third: šalušti eqlim “a third of the field” — the widow’s child-raising portion · also a third of the crop in a sharecrop lease: šaluš
